title: Why Fans Stay: The Psychology of Supporting Rajasthan Royals Through Losing Seasons
dek: Supporting Rajasthan Royals has meant living through losing seasons as well as good ones. The record shows how often a bad year has been followed by a better one.
excerpt: Rajasthan Royals have had losing seasons, and most were followed by something better. That pattern of recovery is the most measurable reason a fan stays.

sections.heading: Staying Through the Bad Years
body: Fans do not choose their team by its results, and most do not leave because of them. The psychology of loyalty involves identity, family and place far more than the points table.
The CricField warehouse holds no survey, sentiment or social-media data, so it cannot measure what fans feel. It can measure what they have watched.

sections.heading: How Often the Bad Years Come
body: Rajasthan Royals have won fewer than half their decided matches in {{ev:ws-losing}} of {{ev:ws-n-seasons}} seasons. The chart shows every season's win rate.
Those are the seasons in which loyalty is tested hardest.

sections.heading: What Followed
body: {{ev:ws-improved}} of the {{ev:ws-after}} losing seasons that have a following season in the data were followed by a better one, and {{ev:ws-po-after}} by a playoff place.
Some of that recovery is the ordinary pull of results back towards average, not only planning.

sections.heading: Hope as a Habit
body: If bad seasons are usually followed by better ones, a fan who stays is rarely kept waiting long. That record may be part of why loyalty survives.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Recovery Keeps the Faith
body: Rajasthan Royals' losing seasons have mostly been followed by better ones. The record gives fans a reason to stay that does not depend on any single season.
Measuring loyalty itself would need attendance and membership data through those years.
